item.title: 【回复】@ArtificialAnlys：Artificial Analysis公布编码智能体基准测试中不同模型的工具调用次数与Shell命令占比数据
item.description:
回复 @ArtificialAnlys
No single harness is best across models. Performance depends on the harness and model as a pair, and 9 of the 13 harnesses move three or more places between GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3-Flash.

回复 @ArtificialAnlys
Token Usage per Task ranges from 5.6M in Pi to 27M in Muse Code for GPT-6 Luna, and from 10M in Mistral Vibe to 26M in Devin CLI for GLM-5.3-Flash. Pi uses the fewest tokens with GPT-6 Luna and the second fewest with GLM-5.3-Flash, and costs the least per task with GPT-6 Luna, at $0.11.

The most expensive harness scores 3 points below the highest-scoring one with each model: Muse Code at $0.62 per task with GPT-6 Luna (23), and Devin CLI at $0.91 with GLM-5.3-Flash (36).

回复 @ArtificialAnlys
GLM-5.3-Flash reasons differently inside Codex, and we believe this contributes to its lowest performance occurring in the Codex harness. In Codex, it writes terse, telegraphic fragments from its first step. In the other 12 harnesses, it reasons in full prose.

In Codex, GLM-5.3-Flash uses ~220 reasoning tokens per tool call, compared with 400 to 790 in the other harnesses, and produces 52k output tokens per task, compared with 97k to 202k. It scores 22% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 in Codex, compared with 27% to 42% in the other harnesses.

回复 @ArtificialAnlys
Codex's prompt contains no instruction to reason this way. In controlled replays of the first turn, the definition of Codex's exec_command shell tool alone switches the style on (12 of 12 samples), and Claude Code's tools do not (0 of 11).

The style closely resembles the reasoning of OpenAI's open weights gpt-oss models. A classifier trained to separate gpt-oss reasoning from GLM-5.3-Flash reasoning in Claude Code labels 98% of GLM-5.3-Flash reasoning in Codex as gpt-oss-like, compared with 0.5% in OpenCode.

GLM-5.3-Flash is not the only model that reasons differently in Codex. In first-turn tests, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiMo v2.6 Pro switch to the same terse style when given Codex's request, and reason in full prose when given Claude Code's. Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max reason the same way in both.

回复 @ArtificialAnlys
The two models use the same harnesses differently. GPT-6 Luna makes from 71 tool calls per task in Devin CLI to 296 in Muse Code. In Muse Code, Kimi Code CLI and DeepSeek Harness, subagents make 118, 156 and 92 of its calls. In Kimi Code CLI and DeepSeek Harness, subagents make 12 and 5 of GLM-5.3-Flash's calls.

Across the 13 harnesses, shell commands are a median of 34% of GPT-6 Luna's tool calls, with file read and search tools making up most of the rest. For GLM-5.3-Flash, the median is 76%.

item.title: @ArtificialAnlys：Artificial Analysis发布编码智能体基准测试：评估不同运行框架对模型成本与性能的影响
item.description:
Launching Harness Comparisons on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index: the best harness varies between models, and harness choice has a greater impact on cost than score

Harness Comparisons hold the model fixed and change only the harness, to show how the harness affects a model's performance. We ran @OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and @Zai_org's GLM-5.3-Flash at max reasoning effort in 13 harnesses each, across v2.1 of the Coding Agent Index.

Key takeaways:

➤ No single harness is best across models: performance depends on the harness and model as a pair. GPT-6 Luna scores highest in Codex (26), OpenAI's own harness, which ranks last with GLM-5.3-Flash. GLM-5.3-Flash scores highest in Claude Code (39), which ranks 6th with GPT-6 Luna

➤ The harnesses that offer the best performance per dollar differ by model: with GPT-6 Luna they are Pi (21 at $0.11 per task), mini-swe-agent (25 at $0.16) and Codex (26 at $0.19). With GLM-5.3-Flash they are Mistral Vibe (37 at $0.38), Kimi Code CLI (37 at $0.56) and Claude Code (39 at $0.58). No harness is on the Pareto frontier for both models

➤ The harness has a greater impact on cost than score: 11 of 13 harnesses score 20 to 26 with GPT-6 Luna and 10 of 13 score 35 to 39 with GLM-5.3-Flash. Cost per task ranges from $0.11 in Pi to $0.62 in Muse Code with GPT-6 Luna, and from $0.38 in Mistral Vibe to $0.91 in Devin CLI with GLM-5.3-Flash

➤ GLM-5.3-Flash reasons differently inside Codex: it reasons in terse fragments in Codex and in full prose in the other 12 harnesses, and produces 52k output tokens per task in Codex, compared with 97k to 202k elsewhere. We believe this contributes to its lowest performance occurring in the Codex harness

item.title: @mingchikuo：Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and remaining market uncertainties
item.description:
Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO:

1. Uncertainty removed:
Mainly company strategy, product roadmap, tech development, and supply chain management. This overhang weighed on tech stocks over the past 1–2 weeks, so shares surged as soon as it was removed. But whether they return to prior highs depends not only on each company's position in the AI supply chain and Nvidia's ecosystem, but also on the two points below.

2. Uncertainties that remain:
(1) Sales: The impact on Nvidia's shipments and revenue after tighter US controls on AI GPU exports and overseas compute leasing.
(2) Circular financing: The impact of higher compliance costs and stricter reviews on ongoing and future deals.
(3) Investigations, lawsuits, and stricter oversight: Jensen and Nvidia are still under investigation. Future public comments, internal decisions, and external interactions will all become part of the investigation and new evidence for questioning. This also adds to the sales and circular financing uncertainty above.

3. Real-world bottlenecks that can't be changed:
(1) Data center buildout challenges (power, labor, etc.) and stricter related regulations ahead.
(2) CSP capex peaking one by one in 2027–2028.
(3) Manufacturing tech limits (e.g., next-gen advanced packaging yields).

item.title: @mingchikuo：黄仁勳恢复Nvidia CEO职务：不确定性解除推动股价大涨，但仍面临出口管制与诉讼等挑战
item.description:
黃仁勳恢復 Nvidia CEO 職位的分析：

1. 被移除的不確定性：
主要是公司策略、產品規劃、技術發展與供應鏈管理等。上述不確定性曾在過去 1-2 週對科技股造成壓力，因此不確定性被移除後股價立刻大漲。但能否回到過去股價高點，除了取決於個別公司在 AI 供應鏈與 Nvidia 生態體系的定位外，還要看以下兩點。

2. 仍存在的不確定性：
(1) 銷售面：在美國更嚴格管制 AI GPU 出口與海外算力租賃後，對 Nvidia 出貨與營收造成的影響。
(2) 循環融資：更高合規成本與更嚴格審核機制下，對進行中的循環融資與未來新案的影響。
(3) 調查訴訟與更嚴格的監管：黃仁勳與 Nvidia 仍在接受調查中，未來的公開發言、內部決策與對外互動，都會被納入後續調查並成為質詢的新證據，而這也會強化上述銷售面與循環融資的不確定性。

3. 無法被改變的現實瓶頸：
(1) 資料中心建置的挑戰 (包括供電、人力等)，與未來相關法規更趨於嚴格。
(2) CSP 資本支出陸續在 2027‒2028 見頂。
(3) 製造技術限制 (如次世代先進封裝良率等)。

We are publishing 4 new benchmark reviews: 1 benchmark is Verified, 3 are Flawed. Another 4 benchmarks lacked sufficient information to assign a verdict.

🟩 Verified: the benchmark can broadly be interpreted as described by the developer, and any errors don’t substantially affect results. We publish a full review, including weaknesses and limitations.

🟥 Flawed: the benchmark has one or more substantive flaws users need to know about to interpret results, most often >20% of tasks with accuracy-impacting errors. We publish a limited write-up of the flaws.

⬛ Not Enough Info: we couldn’t access enough to assign a verdict. Developers get a week to respond before we apply this label.

Details from Verified and Flawed reviews are below, along with a link to our full rubric.

ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive reasoning benchmark designed to measure AI agents’ ability to explore new environments and adapt their strategy across increasingly difficult levels of multiple games. It is scored via action efficiency relative to a variable human baseline, but models are never told to be action efficient.

This means it measures a mixture of capability and propensity towards efficiency. Overall, it failed our criteria for scoring, benchmark consistency, model elicitation (in the official ‘Standard’ harness), and bias in evaluation setup and earned a Flawed designation.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/arc-agi-3/review
原帖

Qualcomm's core skills still have room to run with robotics, personal AI devices, XR and PC. Patience is key as no one knows when these will be inflected. But, Qualcomm has the right ingredients to be a share gainer in these segments.

As per China, it's been a bear case for Qualcomm as long as they lived. People predicted Qualcomm's China business death since CDMA days but still going strong. Eventually they may lose some of it due to localization but it can be offset by growth elsewhere.

item.title: 【回复】@mustafasuleyman：微软AI发布关于前沿模型预训练进展的官方公告与新闻动态
item.description:
回复 @mustafasuleyman
We fully support OpenAI's transparency initiative. Thanks to @merettm @markchen90 @gdb @sama for leading the way.

We all got into this field to build safe AGI that is genuinely good for humanity. One of the hardest parts of AI safety is coordination, and this is a step in the right direction. Many more steps like this will be needed to deliver safe, contained, and aligned AGI in the next few years.

We're committed to sharing our pre-training progress on a common held-out evaluation set. With OpenAI's permission, we report MAI-2 Base on their evaluation set. Its log-perplexity is 0.819, putting it in the same ballpark as the GPT-5.6 Sol base model. Our model uses the same tokenizer as OpenAI, so the numbers are directly comparable.

In the future, to be able to compare across labs we might need to report bits-per-byte (BPB) rather than perplexity since different labs use different tokenizers. We will also need different evaluation datasets - the fact we have access to OpenAI's evaluation dataset is a special case.

Safety and alignment is now the mission. It's the absolute number one most important focus for our industry. And it begins with small, practical steps like these towards better coordination on pacing.

item.title: @gdb：OpenAI发布预训练透明度文章，提议基于困惑度等指标建立行业共享安全红线
item.description:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

@merettm：We decided to provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI for the sake of moving toward shared safety bars. In “Perplexity and Intelligence” I argue for common limits based on perplexity and other measurements, with progress beyond them gated on our ability to understand AI behavior.
